text.en: Some microbes are friends and others cause disease, and you can tell them apart by their shape.

The aim is to identify bacteria and a virus using photographs, pictures, permanent slides, models or charts. The given microbes are Escherichia coli, Vibrio cholerae, Lactobacillus and the retrovirus (HIV).
Observe each with a compound microscope or chart, draw a neat labelled diagram, write the shape of the bacterium or virus, mention its structural details and say whether it is useful or causes a disease.
Lactobacillus is a useful bacterium (it helps in curd formation), while Vibrio cholerae causes cholera. Always handle slides carefully.
